review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

1:1.sourceText: Παῦλος καὶ Σιλουανὸς καὶ Τιμόθεος τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ Θεσσαλονικέων ἐν Θεῷ Πατρὶ ἡμῶν καὶ Κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ·
1:1.targetText: Paul, and Silvanus, and Timotheus, to the assembly of Thessalonians in God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ:

1:2.sourceText: χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
1:2.targetText: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ!

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness difference: LSV our Father follows the additional TR ἡμῶν; N1904 has Πατρός without a first-person possessive in this verse.

1:3.sourceText: Εὐχαριστεῖν ὀφείλομεν τῷ Θεῷ πάντοτε περὶ ὑμῶν, ἀδελφοί, καθὼς ἄξιόν ἐστιν, ὅτι ὑπεραυξάνει ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν καὶ πλεονάζει ἡ ἀγάπη ἑνὸς ἑκάστου πάντων ὑμῶν εἰς ἀλλήλους,
1:3.targetText: We always ought to give thanks to God for you, brothers, as it is fitting, because your faith increases greatly, and the love of each one of you all abounds to one another,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

1:4.sourceText: ὥστε αὐτοὺς ἡμᾶς ἐν ὑμῖν ἐνκαυχᾶσθαι ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τοῦ Θεοῦ ὑπὲρ τῆς ὑπομονῆς ὑμῶν καὶ πίστεως ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς διωγμοῖς ὑμῶν καὶ ταῖς θλίψεσιν αἷς ἀνέχεσθε,
1:4.targetText: so that we ourselves glory in you in the assemblies of God, for your endurance and faith in all your persecutions and tribulations that you bear—

groups.note: The accusative ἡμᾶς is the subject of the infinitive glory/boast after so that; English gives the nominative we in the equivalent finite clause.

1:5.sourceText: ἔνδειγμα τῆς δικαίας κρίσεως τοῦ Θεοῦ, εἰς τὸ καταξιωθῆναι ὑμᾶς τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὑπὲρ ἧς καὶ πάσχετε,
1:5.targetText: a token of the righteous judgment of God, for your being counted worthy of the Kingdom of God, for which you also suffer,

groups.note: The accusative subject ὑμᾶς of the passive infinitive is rendered as your before the English gerund being counted worthy; the same recipients remain the ones counted worthy.

1:6.sourceText: εἴπερ δίκαιον παρὰ Θεῷ ἀνταποδοῦναι τοῖς θλίβουσιν ὑμᾶς θλῖψιν
1:6.targetText: since [it is] a righteous thing with God to give back to those troubling you—tribulation,

groups.note: εἴπερ means if indeed/since indeed in this asserted condition; LSV renders it since without a separate English indeed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

1:7.sourceText: καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς θλιβομένοις ἄνεσιν μεθ’ ἡμῶν, ἐν τῇ ἀποκαλύψει τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ μετ’ ἀγγέλων δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ
1:7.targetText: and to you who are troubled—rest with us in the revelation of the Lord Jesus from Heaven, with messengers of His power,

1:8.sourceText: ἐν πυρὶ φλογός, διδόντος ἐκδίκησιν τοῖς μὴ εἰδόσιν Θεὸν καὶ τοῖς μὴ ὑπακούουσιν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ,
1:8.targetText: in flaming fire, giving vengeance to those not knowing God, and to those not obeying the good news of our Lord Jesus Christ,

groups.note: The noun phrase πυρὶ φλογός, fire of flame, is rendered flaming fire, converting its genitive flame noun into an English adjective rather than inventing a Greek flaming participle.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness difference: LSV Christ follows additional TR Χριστοῦ; N1904 ends the title with Jesus.

1:9.sourceText: οἵτινες δίκην τίσουσιν ὄλεθρον αἰώνιον ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς δόξης τῆς ἰσχύος αὐτοῦ,
1:9.targetText: who will suffer justice—continuous destruction—from the face of the LORD, and from the glory of His strength,

groups.note: δίκην τίσουσιν is the idiom pay/suffer a penalty, rendered will suffer justice. The justice/penalty noun and paying/suffering verb form one constituent; this does not assert a general lexical equation pay = suffer.

1:10.sourceText: ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐνδοξασθῆναι ἐν τοῖς ἁγίοις αὐτοῦ καὶ θαυμασθῆναι ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς πιστεύσασιν, ὅτι ἐπιστεύθη τὸ μαρτύριον ἡμῶν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς, ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ.
1:10.targetText: when He may come to be glorified in His holy ones, and to be wondered at by all those believing—because our testimony was believed among you—in that day;

groups.note: LSV uses by all those believing to express the participants with whom/among whom He is wondered at. This contextual passive-agent rendering of ἐν does not equate every ἐν with by.
N1904 πιστεύσασιν is aorist participle, those who believed; LSV believing follows TR present πιστεύουσιν. The shared believing predicate remains linked with the aspect-form difference explicit.
The relation ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς, testimony believed with respect to/among you, is rendered among you; this is its contextual relation, not a general lexical equivalence between ἐπί and among.

1:12.sourceText: ὅπως ἐνδοξασθῇ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐν αὐτῷ, κατὰ τὴν χάριν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
1:12.targetText: that the Name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and you in Him, according to the grace of our God and Lord Jesus Christ.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness difference: the first LSV Christ in the Name-of-our-Lord-Jesus title follows additional TR Χριστοῦ, absent at that first occurrence in N1904. The actual last N1904 Χριστοῦ remains linked to the last English Christ.
